description: Spool writer conformance (spool-format.md): latency bucket index, minute formatting, segment naming, rotation, and minute-window aggregation. `count` means runs. Rows compare as sets (order of emission is not significant).

minutes.name: first millisecond of the next minute

rotation.name: one minute, a few rows
rotation.note: all rows within one minute share one segment

rotation.name: minute boundary
rotation.note: the first row after the minute turns opens a new segment with n=0

rotation.name: 1 MiB within a minute
rotation.note: the fourth 300 KiB row would exceed 1 MiB: it opens n=1 in the same minute; the small row follows it

rotation.name: exactly 1 MiB fits
rotation.note: a segment may reach exactly 1 MiB; the next byte rotates

rotation.name: a line larger than the cap
rotation.note: an oversize line still lands in a segment of its own; the next line rotates again

rotation.name: n resets on a new minute
rotation.note: n counts within a minute only

rotation.name: gap of many minutes
rotation.note: the epochMinute in the name is the append's minute, not a counter

windows.name: two runs and feedback on one window
windows.note: feedback merges outcomes into the runs' window (status ok) and never adds to count or latency

windows.name: dimension sets split windows
windows.note: status, errorClass, arm and model each open their own window; ordering of rows is not significant

windows.name: prompt artifacts split otherwise equal versions
windows.note: artifactId is a dimension: two Team prompts that both have version 1 never merge after a slot changes prompts

windows.name: artifact-aware delayed feedback
windows.note: delayed feedback keeps the stable prompt identity and original run minute without requiring an observed audience

windows.name: artifact feedback in its run minute merges
windows.note: an authenticated run minute equal to the filing minute is normalized onto the observed window, including when feedback arrives first

windows.name: unattributed feedback is ignored
windows.note: feedback cannot create a zero-run row without an authenticated outcomeRunMinute

windows.name: invalid outcome attribution is ignored
windows.note: writers refuse malformed or impossible run minutes, feedback with no artifact, and non-opaque audience ids before a row is created

windows.name: same-minute feedback finds measured runs
windows.note: without outcomeRunMinute, feedback may attach only to an already measured matching run in the open minute

windows.name: late completion never reopens a sealed minute
windows.note: runMinute is feedback attribution only; observations aggregate by completion minute so a sealed SET key is never replaced

windows.name: the minute turns
windows.note: an observation in a new minute closes every open window first; the new minute's windows close at the explicit close

windows.name: outcome names are filtered, values coerced
windows.note: booleans count 1/0; names outside ^[a-z][a-zA-Z0-9]{0,31}$ and non-finite numbers are dropped silently

windows.name: feedback before any run opens the window
windows.note: feedback on a run from an earlier minute yields a window with count 0 (it is not a run), no moments and every measure zero; usageSource defaults to reported

windows.name: latency edges and the sum
windows.note: each bucket counts ≤ its edge; sum is the rounded, non-negative total

windows.name: refusals are rows of their own
windows.note: a refusal is appended as it happens, never windowed; close emits nothing when nothing was observed

windows.name: ephemeral instance closes at invocation end
windows.note: serverless hosts flush at the end of every invocation; a window can hold one run

windows.name: five model calls and two tool calls in one run
windows.note: count 1, agentRun 1, modelCalls 5, and tokensSq over the run's totals, not per call

windows.name: correlated tokens: every moment is its own number
windows.note: input and output rise together, so a dropped product term cannot pass: the three squares and three products are each summed over runs

windows.name: two slots in one run
windows.note: two run rows, each count 1; agentRun 1 on the first only, so an agent-wide total counts the run once

windows.name: two recordRun calls for one run on one key
windows.note: agentRun 1 then 0 on the same dimensions: count rises by 2, agentRun by 1

windows.name: workflow slot, three steps inside a run
windows.note: one tag; three type step rows, each with its own step id in step and the slot tag in tag; one run row; step rows add nothing to the window

windows.name: one-call run
windows.note: observe writes a run row and no step row

windows.name: a step reported outside a run
windows.note: observe with step: one run row, count 1, and one step row with the same totals; tag stays the slot's

windows.name: step name past maxPerRun
windows.note: 32 distinct names stand; the 33rd and 34th are written as other, and a name already seen keeps its row

windows.name: step name past maxLength
windows.note: a name of 65 characters, an empty name and a control character are each written as other; 64 characters stand

windows.name: interrupted
windows.note: an idle end counts one run on its own row, and it is not an error

windows.name: model_unresolved is an error run
windows.note: a release whose model cannot run here is an error row a gate can see

windows.name: whatever a caller hands in, a writer writes counts
windows.note: tool and token counts clamp to non-negative integers, so a row always passes the validator

windows.name: a step's latency sum is rounded
windows.note: half up, as a run's is; the histogram counts the model calls

windows.name: a total that would not be finite is skipped
windows.note: 1e200 squared overflows: that signal is skipped on this row and the others land

windows.name: an outcome that cannot be written makes no row
windows.note: a feedback-only row with nothing in it would not pass the validator

windows.name: a long run stays below the last bucket
windows.note: a 200-second run lands in the 262,144 ms bucket, so p95 does not saturate

tolerance.name: unknown fields are stripped, nested ones too, and never leave the host
an unknown row type is skipped and counted
an unknown version is skipped and counted
a later error class is taken
a later status is skipped and counted: a closed list per row type
a step member on a window row is a crossed row
a line that is not JSON is corruption
a row from another instance is corruption
